sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized pale brown species, the head darker than thorax, abdomen and legs, the wing veins concolorous with the legs, the wing membrane paler and distinctly reticulate. Head large, round (Fig. 19). Compound eyes relatively small (greatest diameter about 0.40—0.50). Antennae long and slender, 15—18-segmented. Radius with 1 or 2 branches, radial sector with more than 6 branches; media running in the anterior third of the wing, with several branches; cubitus with more than 10 branches. Pronotum kidney-shaped, about as wide as the head, about half as long as wide. Tibial spurs variable: fore leg 3, mid leg 3 or 4, hind leg 2, 3 or 4. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 14.25—17.75; body length without wings 8.00—11.00; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.82—2.36; head width 1.67—1.96; pronotum length 0.74—0.92; pronotum width 1.40—1.92.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large to very large; head flat, longer than wide, the sides either rounded or nearly parallel, or slightly widened anteriorly (Fig. 20). Mandibles black, very stout, about one third of the head length. Antennae 15—18-segmented. Pronotum more than half as wide as the head, about half as long as wide, more or less semicircular. Fore tibia with 3 spurs, mid tibia with 2, 3 or 4, hind tibia with 2 or 3. Measurements (mm): body length 9.50—15.00; head length with mandibles 3.36—7.00; head width 1.82—4.00; pronotum length 0.74—1.53; pronotum width 1.20—2.90.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original combination is Calotermes adamsoni Froggatt, 1896 (the OCR mostly reads Proggatt), the heading reads Porotermes adamsoni (Froggatt). Measurements in mm. Distribution: eastern New South Wales (type locality Uralla), Australian Capital Territory, southern and eastern Victoria (west to Castlemaine), Mt. Tambourine in Queensland, Tasmania, Belair and Kangaroo Island in South Australia. The original stresses that the species is notable for its great variability, especially in the size and shape of the soldier head: large soldiers occur in the Otway Forest and at Korumburra in Victoria and in the mountains of the Australian Capital Territory, where extreme variation is common within a single nest. Synonymy: Porotermes grandis Holmgren, P. froggatti Holmgren (nomen nudum and later synonym). The original records that the species is unsurpassed in south-eastern Australia and Tasmania in the damage it does to Eucalyptus timber, and lists as host trees Eucalyptus gigantea, E. longifolia, E. fastigata, E. viminalis, E. rubida, E. radiata, E. stellulata, E. Dalrympleana, E. macrorrhyncha, E. microcorys, E. polyanthemos, E. melliodora, E. coriacea, E. maculosa, E. Muelleriana, E. regnans, E. obliqua, E. pilularis, E. dives and Pinus radiata. OCR problems: the genus name appears as Proggatt/Pore tibiae (hind tibia) and similar misreadings; in the soldier "head., to apex of mandibles" the comma is noise; the asterisks in "9*50" and "3*36" are misread decimal points, read as 9.50 and 3.36.
